calls.head: Scheifele gets company tonight
calls.body: At home, the Blackhawks keep sending Frondell’s line (Bertuzzi, Frondell and Teräväinen) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Jeff Blashill has been giving this group the hard job of facing the other team’s top line. Tonight the Jets’ first line is Connor, Scheifele and Perfetti.
calls.call: The Blackhawks’ L2 (Bertuzzi, Frondell and Teräväinen) spends at least 43% of its 5-on-5 time against the Jets’ first line, against about 29% with no line matching.

calls.happened: Chicago’s L2 (Bertuzzi, Frondell, Teräväinen) spent 75% of its 5-on-5 time against Winnipeg’s L1 (9:11 of 12:14). The call needed 43%, halfway from the 29% it would get with no line matching to its home habit of 57%.

lane.tip: Share of this group’s 5-on-5 time against that line tonight (the filled dot). The ring is the call: halfway from what it would get with no line matching (the tick) to its home habit (the dotted mark), since part of any habit is luck. Reaching the ring holds the call; past the tick is partly; otherwise it didn’t happen.

calls.title: Blashill got his matchup
calls.plain: Chicago sent Bertuzzi, Frondell and Teräväinen out against the Jets’ first line for 75% of their 5-on-5 time, far more than the 29% they’d get with no line matching.
calls.said: Jeff Blashill would send Bertuzzi, Frondell and Teräväinen out against the Jets’ first line again

calls.head: Where the Jets have the edge: the power play
calls.body: The Jets are around the middle of the league for the power play, and the Blackhawks are the worst. It’s the widest gap between these two, though not a huge one.
calls.call: The Jets’ power play creates more per 60 than the Blackhawks’.

surprises.head: Winnipeg brought the hits
surprises.body: Winnipeg’s hit score in the close stretches of the game was 162, against their usual 90 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 45 games.

surprises.head: Chicago leaned on their bottom six
surprises.body: Chicago’s bottom-six forwards played 46% of the forwards’ 5-on-5 time, against their usual 42% and a league average of 42%. A team strays this far about once every 40 games.

story.head: Levshunov ends it in overtime
paras: The first period was a wild one. Connor Bedard struck first for the Blackhawks on the power play midway through the period, with Tyler Bertuzzi picking up his 200th NHL assist on the goal. Frank Nazar stretched the lead to 2-0 late in the period, but Neal Pionk got the Jets on the board less than two minutes later. Ryan Donato made it 3-1 for the Blackhawks just 14 seconds later. Kyle Connor pulled the Jets within one on the power play early in the second, his fourth straight game with a goal. Alex Iafallo tied it up early in the third. Artyom Levshunov won it less than two minutes into overtime. Pionk finished with a goal and two assists.

The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way. The Jets hit two posts and came up a goal short. Spencer Knight made 31 saves for the Blackhawks, and Stuart Skinner stopped 24 of 28 at the other end. The Hawks improved to 3-5-0, still last in the Central, while the Jets fell to 4-1-2, slipping to third in the Central.

items.text: Patrick Kane set the NHL record for assists by a U.S.-born player, passing Phil Housley, with 896.
Frank Nazar has scored in three straight games.
Neal Pionk scored his first goal of the season, his first since Mar 21 (16 games played since).
Both of the preview’s calls held.
